findings.reason: §17 rewrites the evidence renderer's heading walk and rests the whole redesign on there being one identity derivation, so it must fold `_section_key` onto the hoisted `section_record_id` or state, as §16 already does for `is_section_identity` and the two readers in §18, why `ledger.normalize_section`'s display form is a distinct question; otherwise the "one definition of identity" invariant the section depends on is false at the moment it lands.
findings.text: §16 asserts the hoisted `section_record_id` is "the one producer of values that [is_section_identity] accepts", but `evidence._section_key` derives the identical `s5`/`s5-1` key from the same inputs (differing only in its slug fallback) and is used to key runs by section and to build the evidence renderer's section-label map, while `ledger.normalize_section` (reckon/ledger.py:203, delegated by reckon/crew/node.py:752) derives a second `§5` spelling for the same numbered plan section; both are live section-identity readers, and in `reckon/evidence.py` the duplicate coexists with a `section_record_id` import

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 consolidates the scattered heading walks onto one parser behind the single public reader `plan_headings`, and §16 hides the section-keyed digest and the coverage question behind `plan_fingerprint`'s unchanged public signature plus one private helper (`_section_digests`) and one private predicate, so complexity is added behind interfaces smaller than what they hide.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16/§17 hoist `section_record_id` as "the one definition of identity" but leave `reckon/evidence.py:50 _section_key` (an identical `s5`/`s5-1` derivation used to key evidence runs by section) and `reckon/ledger.py:203 normalize_section` (a second `§5` spelling for the same numbered plan section, delegated by `reckon/crew/node.py:752`) deriving the same identities; evidence.py already imports `section_record_id` elsewhere, so the duplicate is live in a file §17 edits.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds no public definition and retires `plan_fingerprint`'s `legacy` parameter, §17 names `plan_headings` as its one added definition and re-homes `landed_section_ids` count-neutral, §18 names its one added definition and retires the private promotion name, and §16's refusal reuses the existing `plan-review-missing` family, so every section that touches a family names what it adds and what it retires or merges.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §16–§18 name the existing mechanism each addition extends rather than describing one: the raw-text span parser `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`structured_section_spans` in `reckon/_plan_html.py`, the identity derivation `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` in `reckon/crew/routing.py`, the prose walk `_AuthoredProseParser` and store readers in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`, `interface_counts.py` for the census rule, and the two section readers in `reckon/crew/promotion.py` and `reckon/doccheck.py`; each is opened and matches the plan's account.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every proposed layer states why the underlying machinery cannot simply be extended: §17 keeps the parser private and adds `plan_headings` only because it crosses package boundaries under the house rule §16 states, §18's hoisted reader is a move of `promotion._plan_remaining_sections` rather than a new layer, and §16 explicitly argues that the coverage predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review` because it joins a set to a union.
